facts.text: Yatesboro was founded in March 1899 as a planned company town by the Rochester & Pittsburgh Coal & Iron Company, built on former farmland.
The town grew to over 250 company‑owned houses, a store, a hotel, a school, and churches, drawing immigrants from Italy, Scotland, Sweden, Poland, and Czechoslovakia.
A railroad station on the Rural Valley line connected Yatesboro to the regional mining network, enabling shipment of over 825,000 tons of coal annually by 1913.
The Mary, Mother of God Catholic Church, founded in 1904 on land donated by the coal company, became a cultural hub and produced several ordained priests.
Yatesboro sits 1 mile west of Rural Valley along Pennsylvania Route 85, at an elevation of 1,132 feet.
In 1947, Yatesboro was one of seventeen company towns sold by the Rochester & Pittsburgh Coal & Iron Company as part of a larger divestiture.
